370463.title: Lamzouri's maximum-order conjecture for Dirichlet L-functions
370463.statement:
Let $L(s,\chi)$ be the Dirichlet $L$-function, and let the maximum range over primitive nontrivial Dirichlet characters $\chi$ modulo integers $q\leq Q$. **Lamzouri's maximum-order conjecture.** As $Q\to\infty$,

$$
\max_{q\leq Q}\ \max_{\substack{\chi\neq\chi_0\ \mathrm{primitive}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)}}|L(1,\chi)|=(e^\gamma+o(1))\log\log Q,
$$

where $\chi_0$ is the trivial character and $\gamma$ is Euler's constant. The conjecture concerns the maximal size of $L(1,\chi)$ among primitive nontrivial characters; the supplied source says that no progress has been made in the direction discussed there.

370476.title: The compatible normal series conjecture for finite groups
370476.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups. A **compatible normal series** for two groups is a pair of normal series whose corresponding factors are isomorphic in the same order. Two groups are **compatible** when they occur as regular permutation groups in a common finite group action, equivalently when they are compatible as abstract groups.

**Compatible normal series conjecture.** Two groups are compatible if and only if they have compatible normal series.

This conjecture would completely solve the compatibility problem for abstract groups. The paper's results construct compatible pairs from compatible normal series, while previous work established compatible normal series as a necessary condition in relevant cases; the converse in full generality remains open.

370503.title: The fibered-knot coefficient conjecture for theta
370503.statement:
Let $K$ be a fibered knot, and let $d$ be the degree of its Alexander polynomial $\Delta(K)$, meaning the highest power of $T$. Consider the coefficient of $T_2^{2d}$ in $\theta(K)$, which is a polynomial in $T_1$.

**Fibered-knot coefficient conjecture.** This coefficient is an integer multiple of

$$
T_1^d\left.\Delta(K)\right|_{T\to T_1}.
$$

The claim would provide a fast-to-compute fiberedness criterion and can be stronger than the Alexander condition. The authors state that they have no theoretical support for it, so it remains open.

370510.title: Pach–Saghafian–Schnider conjecture on decompositions of cliques into k-star-forests
370510.statement:
A **$k$-star-forest** is a star-forest with at most $k$ connected components. Let $F_k(n)$ be the minimum integer such that the complete graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $F_k(n)$ $k$-star-forests.

**Pach–Saghafian–Schnider conjecture.** For any $n\ge k\ge 2$,

$$
F_k(n)\ge \left\lceil\frac{(k+1)n}{2k}\right\rceil.
$$

This lower bound asserts that the construction obtained from the broken double-star decomposition together with matchings of size at most $k$ is best possible for decomposing cliques into $k$-star-forests. The statement is presented as a conjecture in the source; no resolution is given here.

370522.title: Edwards et al.'s distance-2 matching edge-coloring conjecture
370522.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $H$ be a subgraph of $G$. A matching $H$ is **distance-2** when the distance in $G$ between any two vertices in distinct components of $H$ is at least $2$. An $(\Delta+1)$-edge-coloring of $H$ is a proper edge-coloring using $\Delta+1$ colors.

**Edwards et al.'s conjecture.** If $H$ is a distance-2 matching, then every $(\Delta+1)$-edge-coloring of $H$ extends to a $(\Delta+1)$-edge-coloring of $G$.

The conjecture is the edge-coloring analogue motivating the paper's total-coloring extension conjectures. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

370671.title: Kohn-type conjecture for 2-adjacent alternating knots
370671.statement: Let $K$ be an alternating non-trivial $2$-adjacent knot, and let a **minimal diagram** mean a diagram of $K$ with the minimum crossing number. A **$2$-adjacency set** is a pair of crossings in a diagram that exhibits $2$-adjacency. **Kohn-type conjecture.** Every alternating non-trivial $2$-adjacent knot has a $2$-adjacency set in every minimal diagram. This is presented as a consequence of the two preceding conjectures: one asserting that the relevant unknotting crossings remain $2$-adjacent, and the other excluding same-sign $2$-adjacency except for the trefoil.

370701.title: The Schneider–Ollivier surjectivity conjecture for the canonical morphism
370701.statement:
Let $G$ be a reductive $p$-adic Lie group, let $\mathbb{X}$ be the associated coefficient system, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be its Hecke algebra. The canonical morphism is

$$
\mathbb{X}^*\to\mathcal{H}.
$$

**Schneider–Ollivier's surjectivity conjecture.** The canonical morphism $\mathbb{X}^*\to\mathcal{H}$ is a surjection.

This conjecture was denoted by (sur) by Schneider and Ollivier and is described as the largest obstacle to understanding the torsionfree category of $\mathcal{H}$-modules in higher rank. Its resolution status is not specified in the source.

370769.title: Minimum-degree conjecture for minimal extendable claw-free graphs
370769.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimal $k$-extendable claw-free graph, meaning that $G$ is $k$-extendable and deleting any edge produces a graph that is not $k$-extendable. Let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. **Minimum-degree conjecture.** The minimum degree of $G$ is either

$$
2k
$$

or

$$
2k+1.
$$

The paper proves that the minimum degree of a minimal $3$-extendable claw-free graph is either $6$ or $7$, and proposes the displayed assertion for general $k$ as a direction for further investigation.

370838.title: The extremal bound conjecture for the Sigma index of trees
370838.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $Delta$ denote its maximum degree. Let $k$ be an integer satisfying $0<k<5$.

**Extremal bound conjecture.**

$$
0\leqslant \dfrac{2^k(n+m)^2}{2(k+1)\Delta(\Delta-1)^2} \leqslant 2k.
$$

This conjectural bound is used to refine the optimal terms in extremal lower bounds for the Sigma index. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

370857.title: Berge–Füredi conjecture for linear hypergraphs
370857.statement:
Let $(V,E)$ be a linear, loopless hypergraph: for distinct hyperedges $V_i,V_j\in E$, $|V_i\cap V_j|\leq 1$, and every hyperedge has more than one vertex. Let $q(V,E)$ denote its chromatic index, and let $[(V,E)]_2$ be its 2-section, obtained by replacing every hyperedge with a complete graph on its vertices. Write $\Delta([(V,E)]_2)$ for the maximum degree of this graph.

**Berge–Füredi conjecture.** A linear (loopless) hypergraph $(V,E)$ satisfies

$$
q(V,E) \leq \Delta([(V,E)]_2)+1.
$$

This is the hypergraph analogue of Vizing's upper bound for the chromatic index of a graph. The paper presents results suggesting an approach to the conjecture and gives sufficient conditions for it to hold, including conditions involving the Helly property; its general validity remains open.

370867.title: The maximizer conjecture for the Trail of Lost Pennies
370867.statement: Let $\lambda_{\rm max}:(0,1]^2\to[1,\infty)$ be the function measuring the maximum value associated with the game. **Maximizer conjecture.** The maximum value of $\lambda_{\rm max}:(0,1]^2\to[1,\infty)$ is attained at the point $(1,1)$. This conjecture is prompted by numerical investigations of the function and concerns the strength and robustness of the discouragement effect; the supplied text does not state a proof or resolution.

370973.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture
370973.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $p(G)$ denote the minimum number of paths in a path decomposition of $G$. **Gallai's conjecture.**

$$
p(G)\leq \frac{n+1}{2}.
$$

This conjecture is a central problem on path decompositions; the paper notes that it is difficult for graphs with many vertices of even degree and discusses known results for general graphs and Eulerian graphs of maximum degree at most $4$.

371011.title: Vu's sharpened chromatic conjecture
371011.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with maximum degree $\operatorname{\Delta}(G)$, maximum codegree $\operatorname{\Delta_2}(G)$, and chromatic number $\chi(G)$. **Vu's sharpened conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\chi(G)\leq \max\left\{\frac{C\operatorname{\Delta}(G)}{\log\operatorname{\Delta}(G)},\ \operatorname{\Delta_2}(G)+3\right\}.
$$

This strengthens the preceding conjecture in the larger-codegree regime and proposes a bound in the smaller-codegree regime, aligning the former with Vizing's theorem. It is presented as an open sharpening.

371013.title: Square-coloring codegree conjecture
371013.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its **square** $G^2$ is obtained by joining distinct vertices that are connected by a two-edge path in $G$. Let $\operatorname{\Delta}(G)$ be the maximum degree, $\operatorname{\Delta_2}(G)$ the maximum codegree, and $\chi(G^2)$ the chromatic number of the square. **Square-coloring conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq \max\left\{\frac{C\operatorname{\Delta}(G)^2}{\log\operatorname{\Delta}(G)},\ \frac{5}{4}\bigl(\operatorname{\Delta_2}(G)+2\bigr)^2\right\}.
$$

This is an analogue of Vu's conjecture for coloring graph squares and is proposed as an open problem.

371014.title: Folklore extremal conjecture for sum-free subsets of higher-dimensional grids
371014.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $[n]^d$ carry coordinatewise addition, and let $M([n]^d)$ be the maximum size of a sum-free subset. Let $k_d$ be the maximal volume of a region in the unit cube $[0,1]^d$ bounded between a hyperplane $H$ and its dilate $2\cdot H$.

**Higher-dimensional extremal conjecture.**

$$
M([n]^d)=(k_d+o(1))n^d.
$$

The conjecture is known for $d\in\{3,4,5\}$, while it remains open for larger dimensions; a stronger proposed error term is not part of the conjecture recorded here.

371020.title: Logarithmic step bound for the large steps algorithm
371020.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ and let $\vec{\mathbf{v}}\in\mathbb{Z}^{k-1}\setminus\{\vec{\mathbf{0}}\}$. In the Large Steps Algorithm, let $j_{\mathrm{lsb}}$ denote the bound on the largest index used in the resulting decomposition. **Large steps logarithmic-bound conjecture.** There exist constants $c_k,d_k>0$ such that

$$
j_{\mathrm{lsb}}\leq c_k\log\lVert\vec{\mathbf{v}}\rVert_2+d_k.
$$

Consequently, $j_{\mathrm{lsb}}=O(\log\lVert\vec{\mathbf{v}}\rVert_2)=O(\log\lVert\vec{\mathbf{v}}\rVert_\infty)$. The paper proves this bound for $k=3$ and conjectures its extension to all $k\geq 3$ based on computational evidence; the corresponding general result remains open.

371039.title: Smallest spectral-gap conjecture for perfect matching association scheme graphs
371039.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 5$, and let $A_\mu$ be the adjacency matrix of the relation indexed by a partition $\mu\vdash n$ in the perfect matching association scheme. Exclude the trivial relation indexed by $[1^n]$.

**Smallest spectral-gap conjecture.** Among the adjacency matrices

$$
\{A_\mu\mid \mu\vdash n,\ \mu\neq[1^n]\},
$$

the smallest spectral gap is attained by $A_{[2,1^{n-2}]}$.

The spectral gap controls connectivity-related properties of these regular graphs, and the conjecture identifies the relation expected to minimize it among all nontrivial relations. The source gives no evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

371040.title: Largest-diameter conjecture for perfect matching association scheme graphs
371040.statement:
Let $X_\mu$ denote the graph in the perfect matching association scheme associated with the relation indexed by a partition $\mu$ of $n$. In particular, consider the graph $X_{[2,1^{n-2}]}$.

**Largest-diameter conjecture.** The diameter of $X_{[2,1^{n-2}]}$ is the largest diameter among all graphs in the perfect matching association scheme.

The graph $X_{[2,1^{n-2}]}$ is known to have diameter $n-1$, and the conjecture is motivated by the relationship between spectral gap and diameter. The source explicitly presents the claim as a conjecture and does not state that it has been resolved.

371060.title: The homological form of the Church–Turing thesis
371060.statement:
Let $L$ be a physically realizable computation and let $h(L)$ denote its homological complexity. **Homological Church–Turing thesis.** Every physically realizable computation has finite homological complexity,

$$
h(L)<\infty,
$$

and the laws of physics determine the maximum achievable homological complexity. This proposes a physical strengthening of the Church–Turing thesis by placing a homological bound on realizable computations. The source presents it as a research-level conjecture and provides no formal physical model or proof of the asserted bound.

371064.title: Mutation bound conjecture for affine-by-finite admissible biagrams
371064.statement: Let $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ be an admissible biagram with $r$ vertices, with every component of $\Gamma$ an affine Dynkin diagram and every component of $\Delta$ a Dynkin diagram. Let $h_{\Delta}$ denote the Coxeter number associated to the $\Delta$-components, and call a mutation a $\Delta$-mutation when its tropical mutation uses the $\Delta$-term in the defining maximum. **Mutation bound conjecture.** The number of $\Delta$-mutations is bounded above by the number of $\Delta$-roots, $h_{\Delta}\cdot r$. This conjecture extends the preceding root-count prediction to affine-by-finite ADE bigraphs; no resolution is supplied in the given text.

371072.title: Adin–Alon–Roichman conjecture on circular sorting for composite sizes
371072.statement:
Let $S(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ denote the permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, let $[\pi]$ be the coset of a permutation $\pi$ under cyclic shifts, and let $t([\pi])$ be the minimum number of transpositions needed to sort that coset; write $t(n)=\max_{\pi\in S(\mathbb{Z}_n)}t([\pi])$. **Adin–Alon–Roichman conjecture.** If $n$ is composite, then

$$
t(n)\leq n-3.
$$

This is the composite-order case of the conjectured characterization of equality in the general bound $t(n)\leq n-2$. The paper proves the bound when $n$ is divisible by $2$ or $3$, but the conjecture remains open for other composite values of $n$.

371073.title: Adin–Alon–Roichman affine-permutation conjecture for extremal circular sorting
371073.statement:
Let $S(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ denote the permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, let $[\pi]$ be the coset of a permutation $\pi$ under cyclic shifts, and let $t([\pi])$ be the minimum number of transpositions needed to sort that coset. A permutation $\pi$ is **affine** if

$$
\pi(x)=ax+b
$$

for some $a\in\mathbb{Z}_n^{\times}$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}_n$. **Adin–Alon–Roichman affine-permutation conjecture.** If $t([\pi])=n-2$, then $n$ is prime and $\pi$ is affine.

The conjecture refines the claim that the upper bound $t(n)\leq n-2$ can be attained only for prime $n$. The paper gives counterexamples to its affine conclusion, so the conjecture is refuted, although the composite-order part remains a separate open problem.

371096.title: Conjectured Hilbert-Schmidt radius for absolutely PPT qutrit-qudit states
371096.statement:
Let $M_3\otimes M_n$ be equipped with the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, and let $I/(3n)$ denote the maximally mixed state. Consider the smallest Euclidean ball centered at $I/(3n)$ that contains all absolutely PPT states in a $3\otimes n$ system. **Geometric-radius conjecture.** Its radius is

$$
\begin{cases}
\frac1{3\sqrt n} &\text{if } n\equiv 0\pmod 4,\\
\frac{\sqrt{27n^2+6n-1}}{(9n+1)\sqrt{3n}} &\text{if } n\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\
\frac{\sqrt{27n^2+12n-4}}{(9n+2)\sqrt{3n}} &\text{if } n\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\
\frac{\sqrt{27n^2-6n-1}}{(9n-1)\sqrt{3n}} &\text{if } n\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$

This is the geometric reformulation of the conjectured maximum-purity formula for absolutely PPT qutrit-qudit states; the numerical estimates do not establish the formula, so it remains open.

371162.title: Tan et al.'s labeled coupon collector difference conjecture
371162.statement:
Let $Q_I(n,k)$ and $Q_{II}(n,k)$ denote the numbers of groups required to determine all coupon labels when the label set is known in advance and when it is not, respectively. For $k=2$, let $H_n=1+1/2+\cdots+1/n$ be the $n$-th harmonic number. **Tan et al.'s difference conjecture.**

$$
E(Q_{II}(n,2))-E(Q_I(n,2))=\frac{1}{2}n+o(n).
$$

This is one of two conjectures raised for the labeled coupon collector problem; its resolution is not specified in the source.

371170.title: The extremal conjecture for average size of 1-nearly independent sets in trees
371170.statement: Let $R_n$ be the tree obtained, for $n\geq 4$, by subdividing once an edge of the star $S_{n-1}$, and let $av_1(T)$ denote the average size of the $1$-nearly independent vertex sets of a tree $T$. **Extremal tree conjecture.** The tree $R_n$ reaches the maximum value of $av_1$ over the set of all $n$-vertex trees. The preceding theorem establishes that the maximum has the form $n/2+\delta_n$ for $n>8$, with $0<\delta_n<1/2$, and that the bounds are asymptotically sharp; the conjecture identifies $R_n$ as an extremal tree.

371210.title: The Halanay–Smith criterion for strong stability with distributed delays
371210.statement:
Let $M\in\mathcal G$, and let $\Sigma_M$ denote the associated linear functional system. Write

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{HS}}(M):=\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak C}\rho\left(\int_{-1}^0e^{i\xi(\theta)}\,dM(\theta)\right),
$$

where $\mathfrak C=\{\xi\colon[-1,0]\to\mathbb R:\xi\text{ is Borel-measurable}\}$. A system is **strongly stable** if every admissible pushforward $\varphi_*\mu$ is exponentially stable, and **locally strongly stable** if this holds for all admissible pushforwards sufficiently close to the identity.

**Halanay–Smith criterion.** Let $M\in\mathcal G$. The following statements are equivalent:

1. $\rho_{\mathrm{HS}}(M)<1$.
2. The system $\Sigma_M$ is strongly stable.
3. The system $\Sigma_M$ is locally strongly stable.

This conjecture proposes that the spectral-radius condition extends the Halanay–Smith stability criterion from the previously established setting to general distributed-delay systems. The supplied text does not state whether the equivalence has been proved or refuted.

371211.title: Krivelevich–Lew–Michaeli edge-counting conjecture for graph rigidity
371211.statement:
Let $f(n,d)$ be the smallest integer such that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $f(n,d)$ is $d$-rigid. A graph is $d$-rigid when every generic framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is rigid. **Krivelevich–Lew–Michaeli's conjecture.** For $1\leq d<n$,

$$
f(n,d)\leq \max\left\{\left\lceil\frac{n+d-2}{2}\right\rceil,\left\lceil 2d-\frac{d(d+1)}{n}\right\rceil\right\}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is verified in the special cases $d\in\{2,3\}$; the general case is not asserted to be solved here.

371212.title: Degree-sum conjecture for graph rigidity
371212.statement:
For a graph $G$, define

$$
\eta(G)=\min_{uv\notin E(G)}\bigl(\deg_G(u)+\deg_G(v)\bigr),
$$

and let $g(n,d)$ be the smallest integer such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\eta(G)\geq g(n,d)$ is $d$-rigid. **Degree-sum conjecture.** If $n,d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n>2d+2$, then

$$
g(n,d)=n+d-2.
$$

This is proposed after noting that the minimum-degree lower bound gives $g(n,d)\geq n+d-2$ in this regime; the paper does not state a resolution of the proposed equality.

371232.title: Erdős–Falconer distance conjecture in even-dimensional finite vector spaces
371232.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let $d\geq 2$ be even, and equip $\mathbb{F}_q^d$ with the quadratic form

$$
\|\mathbf{x}\|:=x_1^2+\cdots+x_d^2.
$$

For $E\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^d$, define its distance set by

$$
\Delta(E):=\{\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|:\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in E\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q.
$$

Let $\alpha(d)$ be the smallest exponent such that whenever $E\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^d$ satisfies $|E|\gg q^{\alpha(d)}$, one has $|\Delta(E)|\gg q$. **Erdős–Falconer distance conjecture.** If $d\geq 2$ is even, then

$$
\alpha(d)=\frac{d}{2}.
$$

This is the finite-field analogue of the Erdős–Falconer distance conjecture from geometric measure theory. The conjecture specifies the expected sharp threshold for positive-proportion distance sets in even dimensions.

371289.title: Flandrin et al.'s neighbor sum distinguishing proper edge-coloring conjecture
371289.statement:
Let $G$ be a nice graph, meaning that it has no $K_2$ component. A proper edge-coloring is an edge-coloring in which adjacent edges receive different colors, and $\chi'_{\sum}(G)$ denotes the smallest number of colors in a proper edge-coloring whose induced vertex sums distinguish every adjacent pair. **Flandrin et al.'s conjecture.** Every nice graph $G\neq C_5$ satisfies

$$
\chi'_{\sum}(G)\leq\Delta(G)+2.
$$

This is a proper-edge-coloring analogue of the neighbor sum distinguishing problem; the source states that the conjecture remains unresolved.

371337.title: Harvey's minimum-degree conjecture on chords of longest cycles
371337.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree, and let a **cycle of maximum order** mean a cycle containing the maximum possible number of vertices in $G$. **Harvey's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq \sqrt{n},
$$

then every cycle of maximum order in $G$ contains a chord.

The source attributes this conjecture to Harvey and does not state a resolution. The paper proves related results under large-circumference hypotheses, but the stated minimum-degree conjecture remains open on the supplied evidence.

371338.title: Chord conjecture for longest cycles containing a linear forest
371338.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph with $k\geq 2$, and let $F$ be a **linear forest**, meaning a graph whose components are paths, that is a subgraph of $G$ with $l$ edges and $t$ isolated vertices. Assume that

$$
l+t\leq k-2.
$$

A **longest cycle passing through $F$** is a cycle containing $F$ with maximum length among all cycles of $G$ that contain $F$. **Wu--Zhang's conjecture.** Every longest cycle of $G$ passing through $F$ has a chord.

The connectivity assumption ensures that a cycle containing $F$ exists. The paper proves the conjecture for several cases involving a linear forest with at most one edge and sufficiently large circumference, while the full statement remains open on the supplied evidence.

371382.title: Stecher's cul-de-sac conjecture for rectangular-lattice HP folding
371382.statement:
Let $J_{\mathrm{rect}}(x)$ denote the maximum number of points achievable for a binary word $x$ in the two-dimensional rectangular lattice. For binary words $x$ and $y$, **Stecher's cul-de-sac conjecture.**

$$
J_{\mathrm{rect}}(x)\leq J_{\mathrm{rect}}(xy).
$$

This formalizes the proposed weak monotonicity of the HP folding problem under adjoining a suffix; the paper proves nonmonotonicity under concatenation, so the conjecture is refuted.

371384.title: Luo–Tian–Wu's bipartite connectivity-keeping tree conjecture
371384.statement:
Throughout, graphs are finite, simple, and undirected. Let $\k$ be a positive integer, and let $\T$ be a tree with bipartition $(X,Y)$. A graph is $\k$-connected when its connectivity satisfies $\kappa(G)\geq k$; $\delta(G)$ denotes minimum degree, and $\G-V(T')$ is the graph obtained by deleting the vertices of $\T'$.

**Luo–Tian–Wu's conjecture.** Every $\k$-connected bipartite graph $\G$ with

$$
\delta(G)\geq k+\max\{|X|,|Y|\}
$$

contains a subtree $\T'\cong T$ such that

$$
\kappa(G-V(T'))\geq k.
$$

This is the bipartite analogue of Mader's connectivity-keeping tree conjecture. The conjecture remains open for $\k\geq 4$; the corresponding path result is known under a related minimum-degree condition.

371440.title: Palis's finitude of attractors conjecture for interval maps
371440.statement: Let $C^r([0,1])$ denote the space of $C^r$ interval maps. For a generic $k$-parameter family $(f_t)_{t\in[-1,1]^k} \subset C^r([0,1])$, where $t\in[-1,1]^k$ is equipped with Lebesgue measure, call an attractor **regular** if it is a periodic orbit and **stochastic** if it carries an invariant probability measure absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. **Palis's conjecture.** For Lebesgue almost every $t\in[-1,1]^k$, the map $f_t$ has only finitely many attractors, each of which is either regular or stochastic. This is a formulation of Palis's finiteness conjecture for interval dynamics, asserting that typical parameter values exhibit only finitely many attractors of these two types. The supplied context does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

371462.title: The cutoff conjectures for multi-stack and restricted random-to-random shuffles
371462.statement:
Let $d$, $\mu$, $\gamma$, and $q$ be as in the paper's shuffle-chain theorem. Consider the multi-stack random-to-random shuffle chain $\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{shuf}}$ and the restricted random-to-random shuffle chain $\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{res-shuf}}$.

**Multi-stack and restricted shuffle cutoff conjecture.** Both chains exhibit cutoff, with the multi-stack chain around time

$$
T\coloneqq n\log n\cdot\max\left\{\frac{1}{2\gamma},\frac{3}{4}\right\},
$$

and the restricted chain around time

$$
T\coloneqq n\log n\cdot\max\left\{\frac{1}{2\gamma},\frac{3}{4q}\right\}.
$$

The conjecture is supported by the proof strategy in the paper and by the known $\frac{3}{4}n\log n$ cutoff for random-to-random shuffling, but the two stated generalisations remain open.

371473.title: Cubic skein determination of wrapping number
371473.statement: Let $L$ be a link in the solid torus. Its **wrapping number** is the minimum geometric intersection number of $L$ with a meridional disk of the solid torus. **Cubic skein determination of wrapping number.** The wrapping number of a link in the solid torus is determined by its value in the cubic skein module. This would provide a basic geometric invariant detectable from the cubic skein-module class and clarify the module's structure.

371510.title: Dvořák et al.'s star chromatic index conjecture for subcubic graphs
371510.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $3$, and let $\chi'_{st}(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a proper edge-coloring of $G$ with no bichromatic path or cycle of length four. **Dvořák et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_{st}(G) \leq 6.
$$

Although the conjecture remains open, it has been confirmed for special classes including subcubic outer-planar graphs and subcubic graphs with maximum average degree at most $5/2$.

371512.title: Green's conjecture on graded Betti numbers of curves
371512.statement: Let $X$ be a curve of genus $g$. For a divisor $D$ on $X$ of degree $d$, let $g_d^r$ denote a subspace of the Riemann–Roch space $L(D)$ of dimension $r+1$, and let $\beta_{p,2}$ be the corresponding graded Betti number. **Green's conjecture.** One has $\beta_{p,2}\neq 0$ if and only if there exists a divisor $D$ on $X$ of degree $d$ such that a subspace $g_d^r$ of $L(D)$ satisfies $d\leq g-1$, $r=\ell(D)-1\geq 1$, and $d-2r\leq p$. This conjecture relates the graded Betti numbers of a curve to the existence of linear series such as a $g_4^1$, and is used in studying the complex gonality of modular curves. The source does not provide enough information here to determine whether the conjecture is open or resolved.

371548.title: Caoduro–Khodamoradi–Paat–Shepherd's oriented-matroid embracing-distance conjecture
371548.statement: Let $M$ be an oriented matroid of rank $r$, let $e$ be the distinguished element defining the embracing condition, and let $A$ and $B$ be bases of $M$. Call them **$e$-embracing** when they satisfy the source's $e$-embracing basis condition, and let their $e$-embracing exchange distance be the minimum number of exchanges in a sequence of $e$-embracing bases joining them. **Oriented-matroid embracing-distance conjecture.** The $e$-embracing exchange distance of two $e$-embracing bases of a rank-$r$ oriented matroid is at most $r$. In the abstract oriented-matroid setting, it remains open even whether an exchange sequence satisfying the required embracing condition always exists, regardless of its length.
